audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Davidic descendants from Hebron through postexilic generations, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for David's wives and children, Bathshua/Bathsheba naming, Tamar, concubines, royal succession, exile, Jeconiah's descendants, women named and unnamed, and chronological variants.

verses.restored: These were sons of David born to him in Hebron: firstborn Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; second Daniel/Chileab, by Abigail the Carmelite;
third Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; fourth Adonijah son of Haggith;
fifth Shephatiah by Abital; sixth Ithream by Eglah his wife.
Six were born to him in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months; in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—four by Bathshua/Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel.
Also Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet—nine.
These were all sons of David, besides sons of concubines; Tamar was their sister.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam; Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah/Uzziah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.
Sons of Josiah: firstborn Johanan, second Jehoiakim, third Zedekiah, fourth Shallum/Jehoahaz.
Sons/descendants of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son and Zedekiah his son/kinsman.
Sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Children of Zerubbabel: Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister;
also Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed—five.
Descendants of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; descendants of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah.
Descendants of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. Sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six with their father/another textual count.
Sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam—three.
Sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven.

translation_notes: The chapter compresses stories of violence, coercion, grief, and political rivalry into a succession list; Samuel and Kings must remain in view.
Bathshua is generally identified with Bathsheba. Her appearance as Solomon's mother must not erase David's sexual abuse of royal power or Uriah's command murder.
Tamar is named only as sister, but 2 Samuel 13 preserves her rape, protest, desolation, and abandonment. Genealogy may not silence the survivor's story.
David's wives, concubines, and unnamed mothers lived within unequal royal household structures; their reproductive labor is not evidence of free consent.
Royal descent does not establish moral superiority, Divine immunity, or hereditary entitlement for modern rulers.
Jeconiah is named as captive, keeping imperial violence and exile within the family archive.
Shelomith is one of few postexilic daughters named; many women remain structurally omitted.
The final generations contain textual and chronological difficulties and require Hebrew, Greek, Syriac, and manuscript comparison.
safety_note: Do not turn Davidic genealogy into leader worship, Christian supersessionism, bloodline mysticism, hereditary monarchy, or erasure of Bathsheba and Tamar. Names in a royal line do not absolve abuse, murder, coercion, or imperial collaboration.
